parsedVerdict.reasoning: The unit has one file, src/orders/presentation/orders.controller.ts, and it serves one concern: the HTTP endpoints for the orders resource under @Controller('orders'). Every handler is a thin adapter. It reads route parameters, query values and request bodies, then hands off to an application use-case or query. None of them contains business rules or invariants. That means nothing in the file duplicates a rule that should live in one place: state transitions, quantity checks and similar logic stay in the application and domain layers. Reads and writes use different paths. Reads go through the CQRS QueryBus (GetOrderQuery and GetOrdersQuery). Writes call injected use-case services directly (CreateOrderService and the others). This is uneven, but each path is used the same way every time: all reads go through the bus and all writes go through use-case services. That looks like a deliberate read/write split, not a bypass of the module's abstractions. The file also never reaches past the application layer into repositories or domain entities.
